newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts in quiet trade.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps drifted sideways in quiet directionless trade as most players chose to stay on the sidelines in the absence of fresh indicators, brokers said on Monday.
"The market is very quiet with London on holiday," one broker said. "I think people will only come out later in the day when things are clearer."
April gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.80/$26.05 per barrel almost unchanged from Thursday''s $25.85/$26.00, brokers said.
Traders said there are some fears that after today, local trader Hin Leong might stop its month-long support of the gas oil market which led to a more than $3.00 per barrel hike since early March.
Hin Leong bought about 6.2 million barrels in March in their efforts to boost prcies.
Most traders said the volume of physical cargoes purchased suggested that Hin Leong might not be there to buy more as there might not be many buyers left after these huge amounts are placed out.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade was also quoted unchanged with April seen at minus 35 to minus 25 cents per barrel, brokers said.
Fuel oil swaps were quoted down 50 cents in quiet trade with April at $98.50/$99.50.
